\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{دستور} \fa{پخت} (dastur-e pokht)}{دستور پخت (dastur-e pokht)}]{\fa{دستور} \fa{پخت} (dastur-e pokht) — a recipe}

\label{lesson:FA-C355-dastur-e-pokht}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for an inscription, then the Persian for a ruin.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{دستور} \fa{پخت}}
\textbf{\fa{دستور} \fa{پخت}} (\emph{dastur-e pokht}) — \textquotedblleft{}a recipe\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{این} \fa{دستور} \fa{پخت} \fa{را} \fa{از} \fa{مادربزرگم} \fa{یاد} \fa{گرفتم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{In dastur-e pokht râ az mâdarbozorgam yâd gereftam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I learned this recipe from my grandmother.
\end{quote}

\emph{dastur} \textquotedblleft{}instruction\textquotedblright{} + \emph{pokht} \textquotedblleft{}cooking\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{pokhtan} \textquotedblleft{}to cook\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{dastur} \textquotedblleft{}command, instruction\textquotedblright{} is a Persian word that EtymDB lists without a parent, and \emph{pokht} \textquotedblleft{}cooking\textquotedblright{} is the past stem of the native verb \emph{pokhtan} \textquotedblleft{}to cook\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dastur-e pokht}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dastur-e pokht}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{dastur-e pokht}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for an inscription, then the Persian for a ruin, then say \emph{dastur-e pokht} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{دستور} \fa{پخت} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A recipe\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{مواد} (mavâd)}{مواد (mavâd)}]{\fa{مواد} (mavâd) — ingredients; materials}

\label{lesson:FA-C355-mavad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a ruin, then the Persian for a recipe.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{مواد}}
\textbf{\fa{مواد}} (\emph{mavâd}) — \textquotedblleft{}ingredients; materials\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{همه} \fa{مواد} \fa{را} \fa{روی} \fa{میز} \fa{آشپزخانه} \fa{گذاشت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Hame-ye mavâd râ ru-ye miz-e âshpazkhâne gozâsht.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She put all the ingredients out on the kitchen table.
\end{quote}

The Arabic broken plural of \emph{mâdde} \textquotedblleft{}a substance\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Mavâd-e lâzem} \textquotedblleft{}the ingredients needed\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{mavâd} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{mawādd}, the broken plural of \emph{mādda} \textquotedblleft{}substance, matter\textquotedblright{}; EtymDB lists Arabic \emph{mādda} \textquotedblleft{}matter, substance\textquotedblright{}, though not the plural.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mavâd}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mavâd}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{mavâd}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a ruin, then the Persian for a recipe, then say \emph{mavâd} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{مواد} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Ingredients; materials\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پیمانه} (peymâne)}{پیمانه (peymâne)}]{\fa{پیمانه} (peymâne) — a measuring cup, a measure}

\label{lesson:FA-C355-peymane}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a recipe, then the Persian for ingredients.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پیمانه}}
\textbf{\fa{پیمانه}} (\emph{peymâne}) — \textquotedblleft{}a measuring cup, a measure\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{دو} \fa{پیمانه} \fa{برنج} \fa{را} \fa{شست}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Do peymâne berenj râ shost.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She washed two cups of rice.
\end{quote}

In recipes, a cup used as a measure. In old poetry, a wine cup.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{peymâne} is a native Persian word, usually linked with the verb \emph{peymudan} \textquotedblleft{}to measure\textquotedblright{}; EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{peymâne}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{peymâne}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{peymâne}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a recipe, then the Persian for ingredients, then say \emph{peymâne} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{پیمانه} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A measuring cup, a measure\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{الک} \fa{کردن} (alak kardan)}{الک کردن (alak kardan)}]{\fa{الک} \fa{کردن} (alak kardan) — to sift}

\label{lesson:FA-C355-alak-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for ingredients, then the Persian for a measuring cup.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{الک} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{الک} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{alak kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to sift\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{آرد} \fa{را} \fa{دو} \fa{بار} \fa{الک} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Ârd râ do bâr alak kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She sifted the flour twice.
\end{quote}

\emph{Alak} \textquotedblleft{}a sieve\textquotedblright{}. Present \emph{alak mikonad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{alak} \textquotedblleft{}a sieve\textquotedblright{} is usually traced to Turkic \emph{elek}; EtymDB lists no entry. \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for ingredients, then the Persian for a measuring cup, then say \emph{alak kardan} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{خیس} \fa{کردن} (khis kardan)}{خیس کردن (khis kardan)}]{\fa{خیس} \fa{کردن} (khis kardan) — to soak}

\label{lesson:FA-C355-khis-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a measuring cup, then the Persian for to sift.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{خیس} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{خیس} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{khis kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to soak\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{نخودها} \fa{را} \fa{از} \fa{شب} \fa{قبل} \fa{خیس} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Nokhod-hâ râ az shab-e qabl khis kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She soaked the chickpeas from the night before.
\end{quote}

\emph{Khis} \textquotedblleft{}wet\textquotedblright{}. Present \emph{khis mikonad}; \emph{khis khordan} \textquotedblleft{}to stand soaking\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{khis} \textquotedblleft{}wet\textquotedblright{} is a native Persian word whose deeper origin is not settled; \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[(dialogue)]{Words from chapters 348–355 — a review}

\label{lesson:FA-R355-review-348-355}



\begin{quote}
Say the Persian for a fairy and magic.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a fairy, magic, a witch, a treasure, fate
  \item to betray, to take revenge, to fight, to kill, to be taken prisoner
  \item a king, a queen, a palace, a castle, a crown
  \item an army, a battle, a victory, to defeat, to conquer
  \item antiquity, ancient, a civilisation, an empire, a dynasty
  \item an era, a century, a historian, ancestors, heritage
  \item to discover, to invent, to found, an inscription, a ruin
  \item a recipe, ingredients, a measuring cup, to sift, to soak
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A fairy? (\textbf{\fa{پری}}.) Magic? (\textbf{\fa{جادو}}.) A witch? (\textbf{\fa{جادوگر}}.) A treasure? (\textbf{\fa{گنج}}.) Fate? (\textbf{\fa{سرنوشت}}.) To betray? (\textbf{\fa{خیانت} \fa{کردن}}.) To take revenge? (\textbf{\fa{انتقام} \fa{گرفتن}}.) To fight? (\textbf{\fa{جنگیدن}}.) To kill? (\textbf{\fa{کشتن}}.) To be taken prisoner? (\textbf{\fa{اسیر} \fa{شدن}}.) A king? (\textbf{\fa{پادشاه}}.) A queen? (\textbf{\fa{ملکه}}.) A palace? (\textbf{\fa{کاخ}}.) A castle? (\textbf{\fa{قلعه}}.) A crown? (\textbf{\fa{تاج}}.) An army? (\textbf{\fa{سپاه}}.) A battle? (\textbf{\fa{نبرد}}.) A victory? (\textbf{\fa{پیروزی}}.) To defeat? (\textbf{\fa{شکست} \fa{دادن}}.) To conquer? (\textbf{\fa{فتح} \fa{کردن}}.) Antiquity? (\textbf{\fa{باستان}}.) Ancient? (\textbf{\fa{باستانی}}.) A civilisation? (\textbf{\fa{تمدن}}.) An empire? (\textbf{\fa{امپراتوری}}.) A dynasty? (\textbf{\fa{سلسله}}.) An era? (\textbf{\fa{دوران}}.) A century? (\textbf{\fa{سده}}.) A historian? (\textbf{\fa{مورخ}}.) Ancestors? (\textbf{\fa{نیاکان}}.) Heritage? (\textbf{\fa{میراث}}.) To discover? (\textbf{\fa{کشف} \fa{کردن}}.) To invent? (\textbf{\fa{اختراع} \fa{کردن}}.) To found? (\textbf{\fa{تاسیس} \fa{کردن}}.) An inscription? (\textbf{\fa{کتیبه}}.) A ruin? (\textbf{\fa{ویرانه}}.) A recipe? (\textbf{\fa{دستور} \fa{پخت}}.) Ingredients? (\textbf{\fa{مواد}}.) A measuring cup? (\textbf{\fa{پیمانه}}.) To sift? (\textbf{\fa{الک} \fa{کردن}}.) To soak? (\textbf{\fa{خیس} \fa{کردن}}.)
